claim: Transcription is a major source of genomic instability.

source: Transcription-dependent DNA double-stranded breaks (DSBs) are mainly associated with RNA-polymerase (RNA-Pol) arrests provoked by different non-exclusive factors including DNA torsional stress, inhibition of transcription elongation, and formation of secondary structures, such as G-quadruplexes (G4) and R-loops (Chedin and Benham, 2020; Crossley et al., 2019; García-Muse and Aguilera, 2019; Kotsantis et al., 2020; Miglietta et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: G4 are four-stranded secondary structures formed at guanine-rich tracts.
source: G4 are four-stranded secondary structures formed at guanine-rich tracts (Burge et al., 2006).

claim: G4 structures are present throughout the human genome.
source: Present throughout the human genome (Chambers et al., 2015; Hänsel-Hertsch et al., 2016; Hänsel-Hertsch et al., 2018), G4 have been associated with spontaneous DNA breaks, hotspots for chromosomal translocations and several human syndromes (Hänsel-Hertsch et al., 2017; Murat and Balasubramanian, 2014; Maizels, 2015; Puget et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: G4 structures have a significant impact on genomic stability through transcription-dependent processes.
source: In addition, increasing evidence also indicates a significant impact of G4 structures on genomic stability through transcription-dependent processes (Kotsantis et al., 2020; Miglietta et al., 2020; De Magis et al., 2019; Rodriguez et al., 2012; van Wietmarschen et al., 2018; Kim, 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: G4 mapping in the human genome shows a significant enrichment of these structures within promoter and 5′ UTR regions of highly transcribed genes.
source: G4 mapping in the human genome shows a significant enrichment of these structures within promoter and 5′ UTR regions of highly transcribed genes, and several in vitro and cellular studies show that the stabilization of G4 structures by small compounds, G4 ligands, generally represses transcription of genes containing G-rich tracts (Chambers et al., 2015; Hänsel-Hertsch et al., 2016; Hänsel-Hertsch et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Stabilization of G4 structures by G4 ligands generally represses transcription of genes containing G-rich tracts.
source: G4 mapping in the human genome shows a significant enrichment of these structures within promoter and 5′ UTR regions of highly transcribed genes, and several in vitro and cellular studies show that the stabilization of G4 structures by small compounds, G4 ligands, generally represses transcription of genes containing G-rich tracts (Chambers et al., 2015; Hänsel-Hertsch et al., 2016; Hänsel-Hertsch et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: G4 structures located on template DNA could act as physical barriers blocking RNA-Pol II progression during transcription.
source: During transcription, while G4 structures located on template DNA could act as physical barriers blocking RNA-Pol II progression, the formation of G4 on the opposite strand could promote and stabilize secondary structures that block transcription elongation (Gómez-González and Aguilera, 2019; Kotsantis et al., 2020; Miglietta et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Formation of G4 on the opposite strand could promote and stabilize secondary structures that block transcription elongation.
source: During transcription, while G4 structures located on template DNA could act as physical barriers blocking RNA-Pol II progression, the formation of G4 on the opposite strand could promote and stabilize secondary structures that block transcription elongation (Gómez-González and Aguilera, 2019; Kotsantis et al., 2020; Miglietta et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Genome-wide analyses of G4 motifs in human cells indicate that these structures are highly correlated with RNA-Pol II pausing sites.
source: Genome-wide analyses of G4 motifs in human cells indicate that these structures are highly correlated with RNA-Pol II pausing sites and R-loop-forming regions, two different factors promoting RNA-Pol II arrests and transcription-dependent DNA breaks (Puget et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2017; Eddy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Genome-wide analyses of G4 motifs in human cells indicate that these structures are highly correlated with R-loop-forming regions.
source: Genome-wide analyses of G4 motifs in human cells indicate that these structures are highly correlated with RNA-Pol II pausing sites and R-loop-forming regions, two different factors promoting RNA-Pol II arrests and transcription-dependent DNA breaks (Puget et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2017; Eddy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Formation of highly stable DNA secondary structures, such as G4, has been shown to promote the formation of DNA topoisomerase 2 (TOP2)-mediated DNA breaks.
source: Additionally, the formation of highly stable DNA secondary structures, such as G4, has been shown to promote the formation of DNA topoisomerase 2 (TOP2)-mediated DNA breaks (Szlachta et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: TOP2 activity has a major contribution in the generation of DSBs in highly transcribed genes.
source: Interestingly, recent studies demonstrate a major contribution of TOP2 activity in the generation of DSBs in highly transcribed genes (Canela et al., 2019; Gittens et al., 2019; Gothe et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DNA topoisomerase 1 (TOP1) and TOP2 recognize and preferentially cleave DNA at regions forming stable secondary structures.
source: Moreover, several studies demonstrated that DNA topoisomerase 1 (TOP1) and TOP2 recognize and preferentially cleave DNA at regions forming stable secondary structures (Froelich-Ammon et al., 1994; Jonstrup et al., 2008; Mills et al., 2018; West and Austin, 1999).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: TOP1 and TOP2 activities are required to resolve topological stresses resulting from DNA transactions in eukaryotic cells.
source: In eukaryotic cells, TOP1 and TOP2 activities are required to resolve topological stresses resulting from DNA transactions (for a review, see Pommier et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: TOP1 and TOP2 relax topological constraints through the formation of transient single-stranded (TOP1) or double-stranded DNA breaks (TOP2).
source: These enzymes relax topological constraints through the formation of transient single-stranded (TOP1) or double-stranded DNA breaks (TOP2), in which the enzymes are covalently linked to the DNA backbone.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the mechanism of these enzymes.

claim: In humans, TOP2 activity is supported by two isoenzymes, TOP2α (TOP2A) and TOP2β (TOP2B), that are encoded by two different genes.
source: In humans, TOP2 activity is supported by two isoenzymes, TOP2α (TOP2A) and TOP2β (TOP2B), that are encoded by two different genes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about human TOP2 enzymes.

claim: TOP2A plays key roles in DNA replication and chromosome segregation.
source: TOP2A plays key roles in DNA replication and chromosome segregation, while TOP2B is mainly associated with transcription (Pommier et al., 2016; Nitiss, 2009a; Madabhushi, 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: TOP2B is mainly associated with transcription.
source: TOP2A plays key roles in DNA replication and chromosome segregation, while TOP2B is mainly associated with transcription (Pommier et al., 2016; Nitiss, 2009a; Madabhushi, 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: TOP2 are poisoned by small molecules that trap the transient TOP2-DNA complex during the enzyme catalytic cycle.
source: TOP2 are poisoned by small molecules that trap the transient TOP2-DNA complex, also known as 'cleavage complex' (TOP2cc), during the enzyme catalytic cycle (Deweese and Osheroff, 2009; Nitiss, 2009b; Pommier et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The repair of TOP2cc requires a sequential process consisting in the removal of TOP2 protein from DNA through TOP2 proteolysis or nucleolytic degradation of the associated DNA.
source: The repair of TOP2cc requires a sequential process consisting in the removal of TOP2 protein from DNA through TOP2 proteolysis (Fan et al., 2008; Mao et al., 2001; Zhang et al., 2006) or nucleolytic degradation of the associated DNA (Aparicio et al., 2016; Nakamura et al., 2010) and the repair of the resulting DSB by non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) (Gómez-Herreros et al., 2013) or homologous recombination (HR), respectively (Ashour et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Bruno et al., 2020 and Olivieri et al., 2020 have recently reported that the induction of DNA breaks by CX-5461 and pyridostatin may result from a TOP2-poisoning-like mechanism.
source: Bruno et al., 2020 and Olivieri et al., 2020 have recently reported that the induction of DNA breaks by two clastogenic G4 ligands, CX-5461 and pyridostatin (PDS), may result from a TOP2-poisoning-like mechanism, forming TOP2cc, but the respective contribution of TOP2A/TOP2B to the clastogenic activity of both G4 ligands is still unclear.
evidence: This is stated as recent findings from cited literature.

claim: The respective contribution of TOP2A/TOP2B to the clastogenic activity of CX-5461 and pyridostatin is still unclear.
source: Bruno et al., 2020 and Olivieri et al., 2020 have recently reported that the induction of DNA breaks by two clastogenic G4 ligands, CX-5461 and pyridostatin (PDS), may result from a TOP2-poisoning-like mechanism, forming TOP2cc, but the respective contribution of TOP2A/TOP2B to the clastogenic activity of both G4 ligands is still unclear.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

source: Moreover, a recent report argues that cytotoxicity of CX-5461 may rely on irreversible inhibition of RNA-Pol I transcription initiation (Mars et al., 2020).

source: We also report that transcription plays an essential role in the production of TOP2-dependent DNA breaks induced by both G4 ligands.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: G4 ligand-induced DSBs are countered by TOP1 that limits co-transcriptional G4 formation.
source: We show that G4 ligand-induced DSBs are countered by TOP1 that limits co-transcriptional G4 formation and by factors that promote transcriptional elongation.

claim: Cytotoxic effects induced by CX-5461 have been related to rDNA-transcription inhibition.
source: Although the cytotoxic effects induced by this compound have been related to rDNA-transcription inhibition (Mars et al., 2020; Negi and Brown, 2015), CX-5461 has also been shown to be a potent G4 stabilizer and to provoke rapid induction of DSBs through a TOP2-dependent mechanism (Bruno et al., 2020; Olivieri et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CX-5461 has been shown to be a potent G4 stabilizer.
source: Although the cytotoxic effects induced by this compound have been related to rDNA-transcription inhibition (Mars et al., 2020; Negi and Brown, 2015), CX-5461 has also been shown to be a potent G4 stabilizer and to provoke rapid induction of DSBs through a TOP2-dependent mechanism (Bruno et al., 2020; Olivieri et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: CX-5461 provokes rapid induction of DSBs through a TOP2-dependent mechanism.
source: Although the cytotoxic effects induced by this compound have been related to rDNA-transcription inhibition (Mars et al., 2020; Negi and Brown, 2015), CX-5461 has also been shown to be a potent G4 stabilizer and to provoke rapid induction of DSBs through a TOP2-dependent mechanism (Bruno et al., 2020; Olivieri et al., 2020; Xu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Human near haploid HAP1 cells were randomly mutagenized with ethyl methane sulfonate (EMS) to select CX-5461-resistant clones.
source: To do this, human near haploid HAP1 cells were randomly mutagenized with ethyl methane sulfonate (EMS) based on previous work (Forment et al., 2017) and clones resistant to a lethal CX-5461 concentration of 0.3 µM were isolated (CX-5461-resistant [CXR] clones).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: Seven CXR clones showed IC50 values for CX-5461 ranging from 0.22 to 0.34 µM, corresponding to an average ninefold increase compared to wild-type HAP1 cells.
source: Resistance of seven of these clones to CX-5461 was further confirmed by cell survival assays showing IC50 values on CXR clones ranging from 0.22 to 0.34 µM CX-5461, corresponding to an average ninefold increase in the IC50 value compared to the 0.03 µM IC50 on wild-type HAP1 cells (WT) (see Figure 1A and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: CXR clones did not show cross-resistance to nocodazole, excluding a multidrug resistance (MDR) phenotype.
source: In addition, CXR clones did not show cross-resistance to the unrelated drug and efflux-pumps substrate nocodazole (Kasap et al., 2014), excluding a multidrug resistance (MDR) phenotype (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding that excludes an alternative explanation for the resistance phenotype.

claim: TOP2A emerged as the only gene with coding mutations in all CXR clones.
source: From these analyses, TOP2A emerged as the only gene with coding mutations in all resistant clones.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the RNA-seq analysis of CXR clones.

claim: Four CXR clones had a mutation in the ATPase domain of TOP2A (F85I).
source: Four clones had a mutation in the ATPase domain (F85I), while two had mutations in the DNA-binding region (S654N and L703I) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the sequencing analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Two CXR clones had mutations in the DNA-binding region of TOP2A (S654N and L703I).
source: Four clones had a mutation in the ATPase domain (F85I), while two had mutations in the DNA-binding region (S654N and L703I) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the sequencing analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: None of the identified TOP2A mutations resulted in the loss of TOP2A protein.
source: Immunoblotting analysis revealed that none of the identified TOP2A mutations resulted in the loss of TOP2A protein, in agreement with its essential function in proliferating cells (Akimitsu et al., 2003; Carpenter and Porter, 2004).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunoblotting analysis.

claim: TOP2B expression level was unaffected in CXR clones.
source: In addition, TOP2B expression level was unaffected in these clones (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunoblotting analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: All CXR clones presented strong resistance to etoposide (ETP) with resistance indexes ranging from 8- to 19-fold relative to control cells.
source: All CXR presented a strong resistance to ETP with resistance indexes ranging from 8- to 19-fold relative to control cells (Figure 2C and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays shown in Figure 2C.

claim: TOP2A point mutations in CXR clones reduce TOP2A activity.
source: These results support the idea that TOP2A point mutations in CXR clones reduce TOP2A activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the resistance to etoposide, a TOP2 poison.

claim: Point mutations in clones CXR #A6 and CXR #A1 decrease the amount of TOP2Acc following ETP treatment.
source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1, the point mutations present in clones CXR #A6 and CXR #A1 decrease the amount of TOP2Acc following ETP treatment.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the heparin-based extraction assay shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Five F14R clones carried five different TOP2A mutations.
source: Targeted sequencing of TOP2A cDNA in five F14R clones revealed five different TOP2A mutations, confirming that TOP2A is the main mediator of F14512 cytotoxicity (Bombarde et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a primary finding from targeted sequencing of F14R clones.

claim: TOP2A is the main mediator of F14512 cytotoxicity.
source: Targeted sequencing of TOP2A cDNA in five F14R clones revealed five different TOP2A mutations, confirming that TOP2A is the main mediator of F14512 cytotoxicity (Bombarde et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a finding that confirms previous work cited.

claim: All TOP2A mutations in F14R clones were different from those found in CXR clones.
source: All of these mutations were different from the ones found in the CXR clones, which suggests that, despite both acting through TOP2A, CX-54161 and F14512 affect TOP2A activity differently
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the mutations in CXR and F14R clones.

claim: CX-5461 and F14512 affect TOP2A activity differently.
source: All of these mutations were different from the ones found in the CXR clones, which suggests that, despite both acting through TOP2A, CX-54161 and F14512 affect TOP2A activity differently
evidence: This is an inference based on the different mutation patterns in CXR and F14R clones.

claim: All F14R cells were cross-resistant to CX-5461.
source: Strikingly, cell survival assays clearly demonstrated that all of the F14R cells were cross-resistant to CX-5461 (Figure 2D), while showing no resistance to nocodazole (Supplementary file 1), with IC50 values for CX-5461 3.6- to 16.8-fold higher than the IC50 value of CX-5461 in WT cells (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1), supporting the concept that the TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones also conferred resistance to the G4 ligand CX-5461.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays shown in Figure 2D.

claim: TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones conferred resistance to CX-5461.
source: Strikingly, cell survival assays clearly demonstrated that all of the F14R cells were cross-resistant to CX-5461 (Figure 2D), while showing no resistance to nocodazole (Supplementary file 1), with IC50 values for CX-5461 3.6- to 16.8-fold higher than the IC50 value of CX-5461 in WT cells (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1), supporting the concept that the TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones also conferred resistance to the G4 ligand CX-5461.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cross-resistance data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Population doubling time determination of five clones carrying different TOP2A mutations revealed no significant differences in the proliferation rate compared to WT cells.
source: Importantly, population doubling time determination of five clones carrying different TOP2A mutations and flow cytometry analyses of 5-ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) incorporation in CXR #A6 and F14R #C1 cells revealed no significant differences in the proliferation rate of TOP2A mutated clones as compared to WT cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from proliferation assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: The survival of WT and TOP2A mutated clones to camptothecin or calicheamicin was not significantly different.
source: In addition, the survival of WT and TOP2A mutated clones to camptothecin, a DNA TOP1 poison, or calicheamicin, a radio-mimetic compound, was not significantly different.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays.

claim: DSB repair mechanisms are proficient in TOP2A mutated cells.
source: Since camptothecin induces toxic replication-associated DSBs, which are mainly repaired by HR, while calicheamicin induces DSB in all cell cycle phases, which are repaired by both NHEJ and HR (Elmroth et al., 2003; Furuta et al., 2003), these results indicate that DSB repair mechanisms are proficient in TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the survival data to different DNA damaging agents.

claim: The sensitization to calicheamicin induced by an inhibitor of DNA-PK was similar in WT and TOP2A mutated cells.
source: Supporting this conclusion, the sensitization to calicheamicin induced by an inhibitor of the NHEJ factor DNA-PK was similar in WT and TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D) and the kinetics of DSB repair after X-ray irradiation measured by flow cytometry analysis of the γH2AX signal were identical between WT and mutant cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from sensitization assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The kinetics of DSB repair after X-ray irradiation were identical between WT and TOP2A mutant cells.
source: Supporting this conclusion, the sensitization to calicheamicin induced by an inhibitor of the NHEJ factor DNA-PK was similar in WT and TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D) and the kinetics of DSB repair after X-ray irradiation measured by flow cytometry analysis of the γH2AX signal were identical between WT and mutant cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: TOP1 levels were unaffected in TOP2A mutated cells.
source: Finally, western blot analysis showed that TOP1 levels were unaffected in TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from western blot analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claim: The resistance to CX-5461 observed in CXR and F14R cells is not associated with major changes in proliferation or DNA repair mechanisms.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that the resistance to CX-5461 observed in CXR and F14R cells is not associated with major changes in proliferation or DNA repair mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings.

claim: All CXR clones were cross-resistant to PDS with IC50 values 2.7- to 4.4-fold higher than WT cells.
source: Cell survival assays showed that all CXR clones were cross-resistant to PDS (IC50 values for PDS 2.7- to 4.4-fold higher than the IC50 value of PDS on WT cells) but with lower resistance indexes than those observed for CX-5461 and F14512 (Figure 2E and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays shown in Figure 2E.

claim: All F14R clones were resistant to PDS.
source: More remarkably, cross-resistance studies established that all F14R clones were also resistant to PDS (Figure 2F and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell survival assays shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Small-interfering RNA-mediated depletion of TOP2A in HAP1 cells conferred marked resistance to CX-5461, PDS, and ETP.
source: The role of TOP2A in the cytotoxicity of CX-5461 and PDS was further supported by the marked resistance to both CX-5461, PDS, and ETP (as a control) conferred by small-interfering RNA-mediated depletion of TOP2A in HAP1 cells, with IC50 values similar to those observed for mutant cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2G.

claim: TOP2A mutant cells do not have significantly different modifications in response to RHPS4 and PhenDC3 compared to WT cells.
source: Through performing cell viability with RPHPS4 and PhenDC3, we revealed that the TOP2A mutant cells do not have significantly different modifications in response to these two chemically unrelated ligands as compared to WT cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell viability assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2G.

claim: TOP2A is specifically involved in the cytotoxic effect induced by the two G4 stabilizers CX-5461 and PDS.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that TOP2A is specifically involved in the cytotoxic effect induced by the two G4 stabilizers CX-5461 and PDS.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings showing selective resistance to CX-5461 and PDS but not other G4 ligands.

claim: Short treatments with PDS or CX-5461 induce rapid production of γH2AX and 53BP1 foci in human cells.
source: In human cells, short treatments with PDS or CX-5461 induce rapid production of the DSB markers γH2AX and 53BP1 foci (Rodriguez et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2017; Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations and confirmed by data shown in figures.

claim: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441.
source: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441 (DNA-PKi; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), indicating that a substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway, the major DSB repair pathway in human cells (Pannunzio et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunofluorescence studies shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: A substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway.
source: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441 (DNA-PKi; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), indicating that a substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway, the major DSB repair pathway in human cells (Pannunzio et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on the increased γH2AX signal when NHEJ is inhibited.

claim: In CXR cells carrying different mutations in TOP2A, γH2AX production was significantly reduced compared to control cells.
source: First, in CXR cells carrying different mutations in the TOP2A protein, clones CXR #A1 (F85I), #A2 (S654N), and #A6 (intron retention), γH2AX production was significantly reduced as compared to control cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunofluorescence studies shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Pre-incubation with BNS-22 significantly decreased the number of γH2AX foci in cells treated with PDS and CX-5461.
source: Pre-incubation with BNS-22 significantly decreased the number of γH2AX foci in cells treated with both G4 ligands, thereby demonstrating the major role of TOP2 catalytic activity in the production of DNA breaks following G4 ligand treatments.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunofluorescence studies with the TOP2 inhibitor BNS-22.

claim: TOP2 catalytic activity plays a major role in the production of DNA breaks following G4 ligand treatments.
source: Pre-incubation with BNS-22 significantly decreased the number of γH2AX foci in cells treated with both G4 ligands, thereby demonstrating the major role of TOP2 catalytic activity in the production of DNA breaks following G4 ligand treatments.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the BNS-22 inhibitor experiments.

claim: In TOP2A-depleted cells, γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment.
source: Immunofluorescence studies showed that in TOP2A-depleted cells γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment and strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In TOP2A-depleted cells, γH2AX production was strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment.
source: Immunofluorescence studies showed that in TOP2A-depleted cells γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment and strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: TOP2B depletion did not impact γH2AX production upon PDS treatment.
source: In contrast, TOP2B depletion did not impact γH2AX production upon PDS treatment, while it reduced γH2AX production upon CX-5461 treatment to a similar extent to that induced by TOP2A depletion.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments.

claim: TOP2B depletion reduced γH2AX production upon CX-5461 treatment to a similar extent as TOP2A depletion.
source: In contrast, TOP2B depletion did not impact γH2AX production upon PDS treatment, while it reduced γH2AX production upon CX-5461 treatment to a similar extent to that induced by TOP2A depletion.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from siRNA knockdown experiments.

claim: Simultaneous siRNA-mediated knock-down of TOP2A and TOP2B further decreased γH2AX production by CX-5461 compared to separate siRNAs.
source: Moreover, simultaneous siRNA-mediated knock-down of TOP2A and TOP2B further decreased γH2AX production by CX-5461 when compared to the effect of separate siRNAs (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from double siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: TOP2A activity is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands in human cells.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that TOP2A activity is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands in human cells, with TOP2B variably contributing depending on the ligand class.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings from TOP2A and TOP2B depletion studies.

claim: TOP2B variably contributes to DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands depending on the ligand class.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that TOP2A activity is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands in human cells, with TOP2B variably contributing depending on the ligand class.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the differential effects of TOP2B depletion on PDS vs CX-5461.

claim: ETP provoked a strong increase in TOP2A signal that correlated with a similar increase in γH2AX foci.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, B, ETP provoked a strong increase in TOP2A signal that correlated with a similar increase in γH2AX foci (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the heparin-based extraction immunofluorescence assay shown in Figure 4A, B.

claim: CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase of TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals.
source: Using the same approach, we observed a significant increase of TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals in cells treated with CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B), supporting the idea that these G4 ligands mediate their cytotoxic effect through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the heparin-based extraction immunofluorescence assay shown in Figure 4A, B.

claim: CX-5461 and PDS mediate their cytotoxic effect through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
source: Using the same approach, we observed a significant increase of TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals in cells treated with CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B), supporting the idea that these G4 ligands mediate their cytotoxic effect through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed increase in TOP2Acc upon G4 ligand treatment.

claim: 360A is a potent and selective G4 binder that exhibits a lack of clastogenic activity in most human cells compared to CX-5461 and PDS.
source: The bisquinolinium compound 360A is a potent and selective G4 binder that exhibits a lack of clastogenic activity in most human cells as compared to CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of 360A and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced the induction of TOP2Acc by both clastogenic G4 ligands.
source: As shown in Figure 4B (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced the induction of TOP2Acc by both clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the TOP2Acc signal induced by ETP.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from competition experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: 360A pre-treatment did not impact the TOP2Acc signal induced by ETP.
source: As shown in Figure 4B (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced the induction of TOP2Acc by both clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the TOP2Acc signal induced by ETP.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from competition experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Inhibition by 360A pre-treatment of TOP2Acc formation resulted in a significant reduction in the γH2AX signal induced by clastogenic G4 ligands.
source: As expected, inhibition by 360A pre-treatment of TOP2Acc formation resulted in a significant reduction in the γHA2X signal induced by clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the formation of DSBs in ETP-treated cells (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from competition experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 360A pre-treatment did not impact the formation of DSBs in ETP-treated cells.
source: As expected, inhibition by 360A pre-treatment of TOP2Acc formation resulted in a significant reduction in the γHA2X signal induced by clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the formation of DSBs in ETP-treated cells (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from competition experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of BG4 signals colocalizing with TOP2Acc.
source: As shown in Figure 4C (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C ), CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of BG4 signals colocalizing (Figure 4D) with TOP2Acc and induced a significant increase in the percentage of TOP2Acc signals colocalizing with G4 structures.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from 3D-SIM colocalization studies shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of TOP2Acc signals colocalizing with G4 structures.
source: As shown in Figure 4C (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C ), CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of BG4 signals colocalizing (Figure 4D) with TOP2Acc and induced a significant increase in the percentage of TOP2Acc signals colocalizing with G4 structures.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from 3D-SIM colocalization studies shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The increase in TOP2Acc-G4 colocalizations was not observed in ETP-treated cells.
source: It is noteworthy that the increase in TOP2Acc-G4 colocalizations was not observed in ETP-treated cells, showing that the percentage of colocalization does not result from a global increase of TOP2Acc or BG4 signals induced by the different treatments (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from 3D-SIM colocalization studies shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The increased BG4 signal observed in ETP-treated cells probably results from a global increase of DNA supercoiling by ETP.
source: The increased BG4 signal observed in ETP-treated cells probably results from a global increase of DNA supercoiling by ETP, which would promote G4 formation as shown in several other studies (Sekibo and Fox, 2017; Sun, 2010; Sun and Hurley, 2009).
evidence: This is a speculation based on previous literature about ETP effects on DNA supercoiling.

claim: TOP2-dependent DSBs induced by CX-5461 and PDS are associated with G4 structures in cells.
source: Altogether, our data support the conclusion that TOP2-dependent DSBs induced by CX-5461 and PDS are associated with G4 structures in cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the colocalization studies and competition experiments.

claim: PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases.
source: We observed that PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases, indicating that PDS-induced DNA damage is not strictly S-phase dependent (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; Rodriguez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cell cycle analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: PDS-induced DNA damage is not strictly S-phase dependent.
source: We observed that PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases, indicating that PDS-induced DNA damage is not strictly S-phase dependent (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; Rodriguez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that DSB markers appear in all cell cycle phases.

claim: DNA damage induction by PDS and CX-5461 occurs outside of S phase.
source: Using the DNA-base analog EdU to visualize DNA synthesis, we confirmed that DNA damage induction by PDS and CX-5461 also occurs outside of S phase (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A; Rodriguez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from EdU incorporation studies shown in Figure 5A.

claim: DNA replication-independent processes are very efficient for the production of DSBs by PDS.
source: Furthermore, comparison of the number of G4 ligand-induced γH2AX foci in EdU-negative cells and in the total cell population indicated that DNA replication-independent processes were very efficient for the production of DSBs by PDS (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of γH2AX foci in EdU-negative vs total cells shown in Figure 5A.

claim: DSB production by PDS in HeLa cells was strongly reduced upon inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription by DRB.
source: Accordingly, DSB production by PDS in HeLa cells was strongly reduced upon inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription by 5,6-dichloro-1-b-D-ribofuranosylbenzimidazole (DRB), an inhibitor of critical phosphorylations in the RNA-Pol-II C-terminal domain (Yankulov et al., 1995; Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from DRB inhibitor studies shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription did not impede the accumulation of G4 structures caused by PDS treatment.
source: Importantly, immunofluorescence analysis with the G4-specific antibody BG4 showed that inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription did not impede the accumulation of G4 structures caused by PDS treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from BG4 immunofluorescence studies shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: DRB treatment significantly reduced the formation of γH2AX signals induced by CX-5461 treatment.
source: DRB also reduced DSB production upon CX-5461 treatment, albeit to a lesser extent than with PDS (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from DRB inhibitor studies shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Pre-treatment with BMH21 significantly reduced the formation of γH2AX signals induced by CX-5461 treatment.
source: In HeLa cells, pre-treatment with BMH21 significantly reduced the formation of γH2AX signals induced by CX-5461 treatment (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from BMH21 inhibitor studies shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Concomitant inhibition of RNA-Pol II and RNA-Pol I-dependent transcription strongly reduced DSB production by CX-5461.
source: Remarkably, the concomitant inhibition of RNA-Pol II and RNA-Pol I-dependent transcription strongly reduced DSB production by this compound (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from combined DRB and BMH21 inhibitor studies shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Transcription plays a key role in the production of DSBs following the stabilization of G4 structures by PDS and CX-5461.
source: Altogether, these data support a key role of transcription in the production of DSBs following the stabilization of G4 structures by PDS and CX-5461.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the transcription inhibitor experiments.

claim: CX-5461 and PDS provoke a rapid accumulation of R-loops in human cells.
source: In human cells, CX-5461 and PDS have been shown to provoke a rapid accumulation of R-loops (De Magis et al., 2019; Sanij et al., 2020; Shen et al., 2017; Duquette et al., 2004), which have been associated with the production of transcription-dependent DSBs and genomic instability (De Magis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: R-loops have been associated with the production of transcription-dependent DSBs and genomic instability.
source: In human cells, CX-5461 and PDS have been shown to provoke a rapid accumulation of R-loops (De Magis et al., 2019; Sanij et al., 2020; Shen et al., 2017; Duquette et al., 2004), which have been associated with the production of transcription-dependent DSBs and genomic instability (De Magis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Upon RNaseHI expression, there was a significant decrease of DNA damage signals induced by PDS and CX-5461.
source: Upon RNaseHI expression, we observed a significant decrease of DNA damage signals induced by PDS and CX-5461 (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2E), indicating that the production of R-loop structures contributes to the formation of DNA breaks following G4 stabilization.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from RNaseHI overexpression studies shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The production of R-loop structures contributes to the formation of DNA breaks following G4 stabilization.
source: Upon RNaseHI expression, we observed a significant decrease of DNA damage signals induced by PDS and CX-5461 (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2E), indicating that the production of R-loop structures contributes to the formation of DNA breaks following G4 stabilization.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RNaseHI overexpression experiments shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Transcription elongation plays a key role in the production of DNA damage by both G4 ligands.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that transcription elongation plays a key role in the production of DNA damage by both G4 ligands.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the transcription inhibitor and RNaseHI experiments.

claim: shRNA-mediated depletion of TOP1 protein in human cells caused a significant increase in DNA damage induced by CX-5461 and PDS.
source: Strikingly, shRNA-mediated depletion of TOP1 protein in human cells caused a significant increase in DNA damage induced by CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from TOP1 knockdown studies shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The increase in DNA damage signals in TOP1-depleted cells was dependent on TOP2 activity.
source: Furthermore, immunofluorescence studies showed that the increase in DNA damage signals in TOP1-depleted cells was dependent on TOP2 activity since BNS22 pre-treatment in these cells blocked the induction of γH2AX signals by CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from combined TOP1 knockdown and BNS22 inhibitor studies shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claim: DNA break formation upon PDS treatment in TOP1 knock-down cells was impaired by TOP2A depletion.
source: Confirming the role of TOP2, DNA break formation upon PDS treatment in TOP1 knock-down cells was also impaired by TOP2A depletion (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from combined TOP1 and TOP2A knockdown studies shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Enhanced DNA damage production in TOP1 knock-down cells is not restricted to S phase of the cell cycle.
source: EdU staining revealed that enhanced DNA damage production in TOP1 knock-down cells is not restricted to S phase of the cell cycle (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from EdU incorporation studies in TOP1 knockdown cells shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B.

claim: DRB pre-treatment abrogated PDS-induced DNA damage in TOP1-depleted cells.
source: Moreover, DRB pre-treatment abrogated PDS-induced DNA damage in TOP1-depleted cells, indicating that they were fully dependent on transcription (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from combined TOP1 knockdown and DRB inhibitor studies shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The depletion of TOP1 in HeLa cells caused a significant increase in the cytotoxic effect of both PDS and CX-5461.
source: Finally, the depletion of TOP1 in HeLa cells caused a significant increase in the cytotoxic effect of both PDS and CX-5461 that was reverted by pre-treatment with DRB or DRB plus BMH21 for PDS and CX-5161, respectively (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from clonogenic assays with TOP1 knockdown shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The increased cytotoxic effect of PDS and CX-5461 in TOP1-depleted cells was reverted by transcription inhibition.
source: Finally, the depletion of TOP1 in HeLa cells caused a significant increase in the cytotoxic effect of both PDS and CX-5461 that was reverted by pre-treatment with DRB or DRB plus BMH21 for PDS and CX-5161, respectively (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from clonogenic assays shown in Figure 6B.

claim: A key factor in the mechanism of TOP2-mediated DNA damage produced by clastogenic G4 ligands is the accumulation of topological stresses provoked by transcription that are countered by TOP1.
source: Altogether, these results support the hypothesis that a key factor in the mechanism of TOP2-mediated DNA damage produced by clastogenic G4 ligands is the accumulation of topological stresses provoked by transcription that are countered by TOP1.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the TOP1 knockdown experiments and transcription inhibitor studies.

claim: TOP1 knock-down provoked a significant increase of the BG4 signal in human cells.
source: Consistent with these findings, immunofluorescence analysis showed that TOP1 knock-down provoked a significant increase of the BG4 signal in human cells (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 6—figure supplement 3C) with no cumulative effect of PDS and TOP1 depletion on BG4 signal.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from BG4 immunofluorescence in TOP1 knockdown cells shown in Figure 6C.

claim: There was no cumulative effect of PDS and TOP1 depletion on BG4 signal.
source: Consistent with these findings, immunofluorescence analysis showed that TOP1 knock-down provoked a significant increase of the BG4 signal in human cells (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 6—figure supplement 3C) with no cumulative effect of PDS and TOP1 depletion on BG4 signal.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from BG4 immunofluorescence studies shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The accumulation of transcription-dependent negative supercoiling resulting from TOP1 depletion has a major impact on G4 formation.
source: We concluded that the accumulation of transcription-dependent negative supercoiling resulting from TOP1 depletion has a major impact on G4 formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the increased BG4 signal in TOP1 knockdown cells.

claim: TOP1 depletion significantly accelerates the formation of PDS-induced DNA damage signals compared to control cells.
source: In line with this result, kinetic studies of γH2AX production in PDS-treated cells showed that TOP1 depletion significantly accelerates the formation of PDS-induced DNA damage signals compared to control cells (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), indicating that TOP1 depletion facilitates DSB production by G4 ligands.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from kinetic studies shown in Figure 6D.

claim: TOP1 depletion facilitates DSB production by G4 ligands.
source: In line with this result, kinetic studies of γH2AX production in PDS-treated cells showed that TOP1 depletion significantly accelerates the formation of PDS-induced DNA damage signals compared to control cells (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), indicating that TOP1 depletion facilitates DSB production by G4 ligands.
evidence: This is an inference based on the accelerated kinetics of DNA damage in TOP1 knockdown cells.

claim: During transcription, TOP1 activity is enhanced by the BRD4-dependent phosphorylation of RNA-Pol II CTD.
source: During transcription, TOP1 activity is enhanced by the BRD4-dependent phosphorylation of RNA-Pol II CTD (Baranello et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: BRD4 associates with the positive transcription elongation factor (PTEF) to promote transcription and release RNA-Pol II from paused sites.
source: BRD4 also associates with the positive transcription elongation factor (PTEF) to promote transcription and release RNA-Pol II from paused sites (Jang et al., 2005; Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: BRD4 depletion provokes R-loop accumulation that drives transcription-dependent DNA damage in cells.
source: In cells, BRD4 depletion provokes R-loop accumulation that drives transcription-dependent DNA damage (Kim et al., 2019; Lam et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Inhibition of BRD4 activity by JQ1 provoked a significant increase of DNA breaks induced by PDS.
source: Interestingly, we showed through immunofluorescence analysis that the inhibition of BRD4 activity by the potent inhibitor JQ1 provoked a significant increase of DNA breaks induced by PDS (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E), indicating that inhibition of transcription elongation facilitates the formation of DSBs upon G4 ligand treatment.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from JQ1 inhibitor studies shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Inhibition of transcription elongation facilitates the formation of DSBs upon G4 ligand treatment.
source: Interestingly, we showed through immunofluorescence analysis that the inhibition of BRD4 activity by the potent inhibitor JQ1 provoked a significant increase of DNA breaks induced by PDS (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E), indicating that inhibition of transcription elongation facilitates the formation of DSBs upon G4 ligand treatment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the JQ1 inhibitor experiments shown in Figure 6E.

claim: TOP1 antagonizes G4 ligand action through a transcription-dependent mechanism that is related to RNA polymerase stalling.
source: Altogether, our results strongly suggest that TOP1 antagonizes G4 ligand action through a transcription-dependent mechanism that is related to RNA polymerase stalling.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the TOP1 knockdown, transcription inhibitor, and BRD4 inhibitor experiments.

claim: The genetic approach used in this study, relying on chemical mutagenesis in a haploid background, is strong for identifying drug resistance mechanisms.
source: In this study, using an unbiased genetic approach, we identified the TOP2A protein as the main effector of the cytotoxicity of two clastogenic G4 ligands: CX-5461 and PDS. Our study highlights the strength of the genetic approach we applied here, relying on chemical mutagenesis in a haploid background (Forment et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the methodology used in the study.

claim: Despite TOP2A being essential in proliferating cells, CX-5461-resistant clones carrying TOP2A mutations were readily isolated.
source: Indeed, despite TOP2A being essential in proliferating cells (Akimitsu et al., 2003; Carpenter and Porter, 2004), we were able to readily isolate CX-5461-resistant clones carrying TOP2A mutations allowing direct identification of its crucial role in DSB induction upon G4 stabilization.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental findings and their significance.

claim: The nine-point mutations in TOP2A separate TOP2A essential function from its role in G4-induced DSB production.
source: It is noteworthy that these nine-point mutations, separating TOP2A essential function from its role in G4-induced DSB production, are broadly distributed throughout the TOP2A coding sequence and functional domains.
evidence: This is an observation about the distribution of mutations identified in the study.

claim: Resistance to CX-5461 can be obtained through different protein modifications and is not strictly dependent on the catalytic function.
source: This indicates that, as observed for TOP2 poisons in a yeast complementation system (Blower et al., 2019), resistance to CX-5461 can be obtained through different protein modifications and is not strictly dependent on the catalytic function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the diversity of mutations and comparison to previous work.

claim: Four of the eight amino acid changes in TOP2A identified in this work have been previously described and confer Vosaroxin resistance to complemented Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source: Four of the eight amino acid changes in TOP2A identified in this work (P593S, S654N, L703I, and P890L) have been previously described and confer Vosaroxin resistance to complemented Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Blower et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to previous work supported by a citation.

claim: Vosaroxin is a quinolone derivative that acts as a DNA intercalator and a TOP2 inhibitor.
source: Vosaroxin is a quinolone derivative that acts as a DNA intercalator and a TOP2 inhibitor, further supporting the hypothesis that some of the TOP2A point mutations identified here alter TOP2A activity.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge about Vosaroxin.

claim: Some of the TOP2A point mutations identified in this study alter TOP2A activity.
source: Vosaroxin is a quinolone derivative that acts as a DNA intercalator and a TOP2 inhibitor, further supporting the hypothesis that some of the TOP2A point mutations identified here alter TOP2A activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity to mutations that confer Vosaroxin resistance.

claim: There is a differential contribution of TOP2 isoforms to cytotoxicity induced by PDS and CX-5461.
source: A major finding of our work is the differential contribution of TOP2 isoforms to cytotoxicity induced by both clastogenic G4 ligands.
evidence: This is stated as a major finding of the study.

claim: Bruno et al., 2020 have previously shown a major role for the TOP2A protein in the induction of DSBs upon CX-5461 treatment.
source: Indeed, while Bruno et al., 2020 have previously shown a major role for the TOP2A protein in the induction of DSBs upon CX-5461 treatment, the impact of the TOP2A activity on PDS-induced DSBs has not been clearly reported.
evidence: This is stated as previous work from cited literature.

claim: The impact of TOP2A activity on PDS-induced DSBs has not been clearly reported prior to this study.
source: Indeed, while Bruno et al., 2020 have previously shown a major role for the TOP2A protein in the induction of DSBs upon CX-5461 treatment, the impact of the TOP2A activity on PDS-induced DSBs has not been clearly reported.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: TOP2A single-point mutations found in both CXR and F14R cells are sufficient to confer resistance to both CX-5461 and PDS.
source: Here, we show that TOP2A single-point mutations found in both CXR and F14R cells are sufficient to confer resistance to both CX-5461 and PDS.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: The major role of TOP2A in resistance to both G4 ligands was confirmed through an RNA silencing approach in HAP1 and HeLa cells.
source: In addition, the major role of TOP2A in resistance to both G4 ligands was confirmed through an RNA silencing approach in HAP1 and HeLa cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study using siRNA knockdown.

claim: TOP2B is considered as the principal TOP2 responsible for the resolution of topological stress associated with transcription.
source: The main role of TOP2A in producing transcription-associated DNA breaks in response to PDS is at first intriguing since TOP2B is considered as the principal TOP2 responsible for the resolution of topological stress associated with transcription (Pommier et al., 2016; Nitiss, 2009a; Madabhushi, 2018; Austin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: TOP2A is believed to resolve mainly topological constraints associated with replication and chromosome segregation.
source: In contrast, TOP2A is believed to resolve mainly topological constraints associated with replication and chromosome segregation, in line with its increased expression during S and G2 phases (Pommier et al., 2016; Nitiss, 2009a; Akimitsu et al., 2003; Carpenter and Porter, 2004).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Some studies implicate TOP2A in transcription.
source: However, some studies also implicate TOP2A in transcription (Mondal and Parvin, 2001; Ray et al., 2013; Yu et al., 2017) and its activity is required for maximal production of transcription-dependent DNA breaks induced by ETP, a potent poison of TOP2 (Tammaro et al., 2013).
